key_insight: A governed agentic AI system can coordinate an end-to-end biomedical research workflow, from planning and data routing to analysis and reporting, while keeping protected data inside institutional boundaries.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals and research teams run faster, more reproducible genetics and phenotyping studies with human oversight, but it is not a substitute for expert review or clinical decision-making.
method: Integrated proposal review, execution planning, governed computational routing, and reproducible workflow orchestration.
Used scientist-in-the-loop oversight to refine cohort definition and reconcile phenotype discrepancies.
Validated the system in a hypertension GWAS and a secondary drug-induced liver injury prediction workflow.
evidence_signal: In a real-world hypertension GWAS on hospital-linked genotype and EHR data from 286,422 individuals, the system reproduced known loci including FGF5, ATP2B1, CNNM2, FTO, and GRB14, with FGF5 reaching about -log10(p) ~ 70; the secondary DILI model achieved AUC 0.842.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful human oversight, data governance, and phenotype quality control, so implementation may be challenging in institutions without strong infrastructure.
paper_title: NVAITC AI Scientist: A Governed End-to-End Research System -- A Hypertension GWAS Case Study
